prompt: Make the hero section of a landing page for Fernwick, a small tool that sends polite automatic reminders when a freelancer's invoices go unpaid. I want a headline, a short paragraph under it, a main button to start a free trial, a quieter link for a demo, and some kind of product visual built with HTML and CSS. It should feel like a real startup site.
prompt_suffix: Return the result as a single self-contained HTML file: all CSS inline, no external requests, system fonts only. Reply with one ```html fenced block and nothing else.
rubric: One element is clearly read first: the headline is much larger than the body text and nothing else competes with it.
There is exactly one primary call to action; the secondary link is visibly quieter than the button.
The paragraph under the headline has a comfortable line length (about 40 to 75 characters) and secondary text still has strong contrast against its background.
Spacing groups the headline, paragraph and buttons as one unit, with generous whitespace and consistent alignment of edges.
The product visual looks specific to an invoice-reminder tool and supports the message without competing with the headline.
featuring_rule: Declared before any run: rank the 3 without-skill runs and the 3 with-skill runs separately by the blind judge's rubric mean (two passes with the sides swapped, scores averaged), and feature the median run of each arm. The best run is never chosen. The contact sheet shows all six runs.

pairs.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): A looks more like a finished startup site: it has a brand mark, a clear two-line headline with an accent word, and a tilted invoice card with an 'Unpaid' tag and 'Reminder sent' status that fits the product. Its floating badges run to the very edge of the screen, and the 'Unpaid' tag crowds the invoice number, but these are small flaws. B has no logo, and its overlapping cards hide the second invoice's number and amount ('00.00'), which looks broken. B's trust line also wraps awkwardly and weakens the grouping. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): B feels more like a real startup site. It has a brand mark, a clear headline with a gradient accent, a well-measured paragraph, and an invoice card that tells the reminder story well, though the UNPAID badge crowds the invoice number and the floating badges sit tight against the right edge. A has a solid hierarchy and calm spacing, but it has no brand. Its overlapping cards also hide the second invoice's number and amount, and the trust line below the buttons wraps awkwardly.

pass 1 (A=without, B=with): A's layout is clean and believable as a startup site: the headline, paragraph and buttons are left-aligned as one group, and the invoice card shows overdue status and a polite reminder, which fits the product well. B has a stronger, centered headline, but its card has bugs: 'Design work – 40 hrs' runs into '$2,000', the card says 'Paid' and 'Total Due' at the same time, and the 'Reminder sent' badge sits awkwardly off the card's edge. B's outlined 'Watch Demo' button is also closer in weight to the main button than A's demo link is. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): B feels more like a real startup site: it has a nav with the brand, a left-aligned text column with clean edges, and a product card that's clearly about reminders (overdue badge, days overdue, 'Polite reminder sent today'). A has a strong centered headline, but its invoice card has overlapping text ('40 hrs$2,000') and contradicts itself, marked Paid but still showing Total Due. B's light-gray microcopy and paragraph text have weaker contrast, and its large card competes a little with the headline.

pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Answer A feels more like a real startup site. It shows the Fernwick brand, and its invoice card (with an UNPAID badge, client, due date, amount and 'Reminder sent today') is clearly specific to the product. Its weak point is the gradient 'Reminder sent today' bar, which looks a lot like the primary button and competes with it a little. Answer B is clean with clear hierarchy, but it never shows the brand name, and its illustration is generic and looks unfinished: a sketchy bell icon and a placeholder document. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): B looks more like a real startup site: it has a brand mark, a stronger two-line headline, and an invoice card with a client, due date, amount and an UNPAID badge, so it clearly belongs to an invoice-reminder tool. Its weak spot is the solid gradient 'Reminder sent today' bar in the mockup, which looks like a second primary button. B's grey body text is also a little light. A is clean and has a clear hierarchy, but its visual is generic and sparse, with an odd bell icon, and the page feels unfinished because there is no branding.
